Still I walked.
Walk I must.

en.html:
Alone now.
Along the forest path I walked.

Hard going. Heavy body, thin consciousness. When had everything become so terribly cold?

It hurt.
Life was running out.

The heart wanted to stop. I kept forcing it to work, kept trying to live. That was why it hurt. Stop this foolish business, and surely the pain would finish at once.

But not yet.
Until I reached her, dying was not permitted.

en.html:
Strength I did not have, I summoned. Lifted myself. Teeth clenched, one remaining arm braced against the ground.

Stand.
Live.

Only a little more. Until I reached her.
Kanae Ootori.

She was an avenger. The one who would judge Kageaki Minato's crimes. The person who would give him his rightful death.

My life had to be offered to her blade. She would take it on account of the unappeased grief of someone I had killed.

She would show the anger of good against evil.

Justice existed in this world.
Evil would certainly receive its due.

This I believed.
This I wanted to believe.

So this life must end by her hand.

en.html:
I conveyed my hope.
—Judgment. Condemnation.

Whether a voice came out, I did not know. But I felt no anxiety.

She was a pure executor of vengeance. It would be all right.

I trusted her.

Kanae Ootori's personality was probably complicated. My understanding of it was not deep. So much I surely did not know.

Perhaps she possessed an appalling nature utterly opposed to human morality. Perhaps she was a demon with a human face and a beast's heart.

Looking back, there had certainly been glimpses to suggest it.

...But what did it matter to me?

Nothing. So I had not troubled myself with it.

To the very end, he had never protected himself.

He could have fled. He should have understood that he did not need to die here.

Instead, he had stayed and fought. Probably with some thought of protecting Kanae also.

He had fought for the woman who swore to kill him.
Against that very woman he was trying to protect.

And died.

Such foolishness.
No helping it. No saving him from it. Such foolishness.

en.html:
Which one was the bigger fool, though?

He fought Kanae to protect Kanae.
She hid the truth, made him do that, and had him kill her.

Well.
...Same only, perhaps.

Two hopeless fools killed each other. Both dead. Very successful arrangement.

Surely that was all.

Dying did not frighten her.
No complaint about it either.

Living meant dying.
Dying meant living.

Same meaning. Different words.

Life starts from zero, or life goes toward zero. Only that much difference. Between seeking death and seeking life, then, what essential difference was there?

No use getting stuck on so much wordplay. Live rightly as yourself, die rightly as yourself. That was enough.

And this end was undoubtedly right for Kanae Ootori.
For Kageaki Minato also.

Wholeheartedly they had lived.
Wholeheartedly they had died.

As Kanae Ootori.
As Kageaki Minato.

So she thought.

より愚かしいのは、どちらだったのだろう。

　香奈枝を守ろうとして香奈枝と戦った彼と。
　真実を隠し、彼をしてそうさせ、我が身を殺させた
香奈枝と。

　まぁ。
　……同じようなものか。

　救えぬ愚か者同士が殺し合った。
　そしてめでたく、どちらも死んだ。

　これはきっと、それだけのことだ。

　死にゆくことに、怖れはなかった。
　不平もなかった。

　生きるとは、死ぬということ。
　死ぬとは、生きるということ。

　意味は同じ。
　言葉が違うだけ。

　人生をゼロから発したものと見るか、ゼロへ向かう
ものと見るか、ただそれだけの違い。
　だから死を求めることと、生を求めることとの間に、
本質の差は何も無いのだ。

　そんな言葉遊び程度の違いに拘泥しても仕方ない。
　<ruby>自己<rt>おのれ</rt></ruby>として正しく生きて、正しく死ぬなら、それで
良い。

　そしてこの最期は間違いなく、大鳥香奈枝にとって
正しい帰結。
　湊斗景明の最期もそう。

　<ruby>直向<rt>ひたむき</rt></ruby>に生きた。
　直向に死んだ。

　大鳥香奈枝として。
　湊斗景明として。

　そう思う。

　香奈枝を守ろうとして香奈枝と戦った彼と。
　真実を隠し、彼をしてそうさせ、我が身を殺させた
香奈枝と。

　まぁ。
　……同じようなものか。

　救えぬ愚か者同士が殺し合った。
　そしてめでたく、どちらも死んだ。

　これはきっと、それだけのことだ。

　死にゆくことに、怖れはなかった。
　不平もなかった。

　生きるとは、死ぬということ。
　死ぬとは、生きるということ。

　意味は同じ。

　そしてこの最期は間違いなく、大鳥香奈枝にとって

　湊斗景明の最期もそう。

en.html:
She addressed him, though he would answer no more.

We were fools.
Such fools, really.

But this only we could do, no?
Another road we could not choose.

We met. We died together—
And this was the farce we made.

So foolish, so ridiculous. And nobody in the audience.
Only us two.
